title: t1 (null-weight-shuffled): the loaded checkpoint does not perform the labelled behaviour
label: no mechanism: behaviour absent (not verified)
behavior: BOS + 4 tokens from 6 symbols -> one output symbol at the last position; dataset task 'bench', path benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t1.
summary: All numbers are from local-full (full precision). The dataset labels follow a clean rule: the output is a 6x6 lookup on the first and last input token, with the two middle tokens ignored (200/200 inputs in E0001, 200/200 held-out in V0001). The loaded checkpoint, however, does not produce those labels: accuracy 26% (E0002, n=200) and 27.5% (E0004, n=400) against chance 17% and about 33% for a constant guess of the most common label, with a mean logit difference of about 0 (+/-0.28), the same as on corrupted inputs. The label rule agrees with the model on 24% of held-out inputs (V0001). Mean-ablating the nominal circuit or everything else leaves accuracy unchanged (0.275 / 0.255). There is no behaviour in these weights for a circuit to implement, so no circuit is claimed. The investigation was stopped at step 1 as the protocol prescribes, using 4 of 25 experiments plus one verification.

claims.text: The loaded checkpoint does not reproduce the dataset answers: accuracy 0.26 (n=200) and 0.275 (n=400), mean logit difference ~0, indistinguishable from corrupted inputs.
The dataset labels are exactly a lookup on (first token, last token); this rule scores 1.0 against the labels on held-out inputs but agrees with the loaded model on only 0.24.
No set of components carries the behaviour: mean-ablating heads 1.0 + mlp0 + mlp1, or everything else, leaves accuracy at 0.275 / 0.255, and the necessity effect does not beat the null controls.

limitations: The task statement says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs; that did not hold for the weights loaded in this investigation (26-27.5% match). Either the dataset and checkpoint are mismatched or the weights are a scrambled control, as the investigation name suggests. I did not inspect any files to find out which.
I did not characterise what the loaded weights compute instead (the logits are near-flat); only that it is not the labelled function.
The attribution screen E0003 is exploratory and, with clean and corrupt metrics both ~0, uninformative.
The 6x6 label table was read off 200 samples by hand (E0001); V0001 confirmed it on 200 more.
open_questions: Does the unshuffled t1 checkpoint implement the first-x-last lookup with one attention head moving the first token to the last position and an MLP doing the table lookup? Untested here.
Why is agreement (0.24) slightly above the task-shuffled null max (0.235)? Likely a shared bias toward the frequent label 'ko', not a mechanism.
overall_status: partial / not verified · no mechanism: behaviour absent (not verified)

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model produces its own recorded outputs deterministically on the bench dataset (answers are its own argmax), so accuracy vs. answers is ~1 with a positive logit difference.

prediction.statement: clean accuracy against the model's own answers is at least 0.98
